title: When Will Monsoon Reach Mumbai? IMD Revises Weather Forecast, Rains Likely by June End; Check Expected Date - Goodreturns
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has now indicated that Mumbai and adjoining regions of Maharashtra are likely to receive widespread monsoon rainfall by June end. This suggests a further delay in the onset of the southwest monsoon over the city, which typically arrives around June 10-11.
As per the latest forecast, northern Maharashtra-including Mumbai-and parts of central Maharashtra are expected to see more consistent monsoon showers by June 25. This marks another revision in the expected timeline, as earlier predictions had placed the onset around June 18-19, which was later shifted to June 22-23.
Initially, the monsoon was expected to reach Mumbai around June 10-11, but its progress along the western coast has remained stalled since June 8.
According to IMD updates, the western branch of the monsoon had been expected to resume its advance around June 15-16. However, the system continued to remain sluggish, with the weather office later indicating that it could stay stuck near Harnai in South Konkan until at least June 20. This prolonged stagnation has contributed to the delayed arrival over Maharashtra, including Mumbai.
Private weather agency Skymet has also taken a cautious view, suggesting that Mumbai may see monsoon arrival only after June 25. If this happens, it could turn out to be one of the more delayed onsets in recent years. The last notably late arrival was in 2023, when the monsoon reached Mumbai on June 25.
However, meteorologists have clarified that a delayed onset does not necessarily mean a poor monsoon season overall. The southwest monsoon is assessed over the four-month period from June to September, and rainfall performance can improve later if active spells strengthen. That said, a weak or delayed June can still create short-term pressure on water supply, reservoirs, agriculture, and weather-dependent sectors.
In the past 24 hours, Mumbai has received only light and scattered rainfall. These showers have not been widespread enough to bring down temperatures or humidity significantly, although cloud cover has helped ease daytime heat in some pockets of the city. So far, the city has recorded only around 13 mm of rainfall this June, which is below normal levels.

Chennai Reopens 22 Subways Following Heavy Rain and Flooding
Chennai has reopened subways after unprecedented rainfall led to flooding, with efforts involving numerous responders to restore normalcy.

Chennai, the capital of Tamil Nadu, has reopened all 22 subways to vehicular traffic after experiencing exceptional rainfall that caused significant flooding across the city. The Tamil Nadu government reported that over 15,000 workers were deployed overnight to assist in rescue operations and clear rainwater from affected areas. In a statement issued on Sunday, the government noted that water had been cleared from the majority of main bus routes and numerous waterlogged streets.

The rainfall was recorded at various locations throughout the city, with Parry’s Corner documenting the highest precipitation at 36.3 centimetres in just 24 hours. Six locations experienced extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 20 centimetres, while twelve areas recorded very heavy rainfall of more than 11.5 centimetres. The government described the volume of rain as unprecedented, with figures indicating that some areas received rainfall exceeding 30 centimetres overnight.

To combat the flooding, the city deployed a total of 650 electric motor pumps and tractor-mounted pumps to facilitate the swift removal of water from the streets. In addition, a team from the National Disaster Response Force and four teams from the Tamil Nadu Disaster Response Force were stationed in flood-prone areas to assist with emergency efforts.

Ongoing inspections were conducted through the night by ministers, legislators, and senior officials to coordinate the city's response. The corporation established nine relief centres to aid residents in low-lying areas affected by the heavy rain, with food provisions arranged for those in need.

Despite the challenges posed by the intense rainfall, the Tamil Nadu government reported that no fatalities or significant damage had occurred and described the situation as under control. By Sunday morning, the city was returning to a state of normalcy, although water remained in certain low-lying pockets and clearance operations continued. Most roads had been cleared for travel, highlighting the resilience and response capabilities of Chennai’s urban drainage and emergency systems in the face of severe weather conditions.

article_text:
தமிழகத்தில் வடகிழக்கு பருவமழை தீவிரமெடுத்துள்ள நிலையில், இன்று முதல் வரும் நாள்களுக்கான வானிலை நிலவரம் குறித்து சென்னை வானிலை ஆய்வு மையம் வெளியிட்டுள்ள அறிக்கையில் கூறியதாவது, "சுமார் 5.8 கிமீ உயரம் வரை தென்மேற்கு வங்கக்கடல் பகுதிகள் மற்றும் அதனை ஒட்டிய தமிழக கடலோர பகுதிகளின் மேல் ஒரு வளிமண்டல சுழற்சி நிலவுகிறது. இதன் காரணமாக அடுத்த 24 மணி நேரத்தில் ஒரு குறைந்த காற்றழுத்த தாழ்வுப் பகுதி இதே பகுதியில் உருவாக வாய்ப்புள்ளது.

சுமார் 3.1 கிமீ உயரத்தில் தென்மேற்கு வங்கக்கடல் பகுதிகள் மற்றும் அதனை ஒட்டிய தமிழக கடலோர பகுதிகளின் மேல் நிலவும் வளிமண்டல சுழற்சியிலிருந்து வடக்கு கடலோர ஆந்திரா பகுதிகள் வரை ஒரு காற்றழுத்த தாழ்வு பாதை (Trough) நிலவுகிறது.

தமிழகத்தில் கனமழைக்கான எச்சரிக்கை
இன்றைய தினம் (21-10-2026) தூத்துக்குடி, திருநெல்வேலி மற்றும் கன்னியாகுமரி மாவட்டங்களில் ஓரிரு இடங்களில் இடி மின்னல் மற்றும் பலத்த காற்றுடன் (மணிக்கு 40 முதல் 50 கிலோ மீட்டர் வேகத்தில்) கூடிய கன முதல் மிக கன மழை பெய்யக்கூடும். நீலகிரி, கோயம்புத்தூர், ஈரோடு, திருப்பூர், நாமக்கல், கரூர், தேனி, திண்டுக்கல், தென்காசி, மதுரை, விருதுநகர், புதுக்கோட்டை, தஞ்சாவூர், திருவாரூர், நாகப்பட்டினம், மயிலாடுதுறை, புதுக்கோட்டை, சிவகங்கை மற்றும் ராமநாதபுரம் மாவட்டங்களில் ஓரிரு இடங்களிலும், காரைக்கால் பகுதிகளிலும் இடி மின்னல் மற்றும் பலத்த காற்றுடன் கூடிய கன மழை பெய்யக்கூடும். ஏனைய தமிழகத்தில் அநேக இடங்களிலும், புதுவையிலும் இடி மின்னல் மற்றும் பலத்த காற்றுடன் கூடிய மிதமான மழை பெய்யக்கூடும்.
